newsitem.title: USA: ITT Hartford sees double-digit growth.
newsitem.headline: ITT Hartford sees double-digit growth.

text.p: ITT Hartford Group Inc Chairman Donald Frahm expects the company to post double-digit earnings growth in 1996 and 1997, he told Reuters in an interview Friday.
"We continue to look for double-digit growth in our earnings," he said. "That's an overall target for the whole company."
Frahm did not provide specific figures.
"In 1997, I anticipate that our life company will continue to grow, both top-line and bottom-line, faster than the industry."
ITT Hartford had revenues of $12.2 billion in 1995.
Frahm said the company is aggressively expanding the commercial affinity and reinsurance arms of its business.
"We expect 1997 is going to be a very good year for us from the reinsurance standpoint," he said.
ITT Hartford is considering growth by acquisition, particularly in Asia.

"We think our best opportunities as a company are in international. We've been expanding primarily in Latin America and Europe, and will continue to look for ways to expand. We're now looking more aggressively at the Far East."
As it nears the December 19 anniversary of its spinoff from ITT Corp, the company is considering dropping the "ITT" from its name, said Frahm.
"It causes confusion," he said. "We're addressing that issue right now."
Frahm plans to retire as chairman of the 186-year-old company on January 31, 1997, shortly after he turns 65.
Frahm has been chairman since 1988. "I'll stay on the board (of directors) as long as they'll re-elect me," he said.
He will be succeeded by Ramani Ayer, 49.
